verdict.rationale: Cal.com's open source is available through Cal.diy, an official GitHub repo that is 100% MIT-licensed and needs no license key. However, it is described as a fork with all enterprise and commercial code removed, so the readable source does not cover the full commercial Cal.com product. Community comments mention an AGPL license and a past community edition, but the current openness of the main Cal.com codebase is not documented in the pack. Missing for 10: evidence that the full Cal.com product source (including enterprise features) is readable under an open license, and first-party docs clarifying the licensing of the main repo.
